title: How to invest using AI, step by step
summary: Choose how much you want to decide, then use AI to research and watch your investments while you make the calls.
body_markdown:
## How do you invest using AI, step by step?


### 1. Decide how much you want to decide


If you’d rather not pick investments, a robo-advisor builds a portfolio of funds from your answers about goals and risk and keeps it on target. SoFi’s Form CRS says its robo-advisor can buy or sell in your account without first asking your permission, which is what that kind of service is for. If you want to keep choosing, look for tools that explain and recommend but leave every trade to you.


### 2. Put every account in one view


AI can only help with what it can see. Most investing apps connect through Plaid, which says it can share an investment account’s balances, holdings and transactions. Include old 401(k)s, IRAs, company stock and crypto, because a fund that looks fine in one account can double up on something you own in another.


Astor connects to brokerage, retirement and crypto accounts at most major US institutions through Plaid, or you can add holdings by hand or from a screenshot. It can see your holdings but can’t move money. Here’s[what to check before you connect](https://www.astor.app/blog/is-it-safe-to-connect-your-brokerage-account) .


### 3. Ask it to explain what you own


Start with your own portfolio rather than the market. Ask how much of your money rides on your largest position, whether two of your funds hold the same companies, and what your mix of stocks, bonds and cash looks like across every account. Those are the questions a[portfolio review](https://www.astor.app/blog/how-to-actually-review-your-investment-portfolio) should answer, and AI turns them into a short conversation.


With Astor you can ask about your actual holdings, the markets or any stock on every plan, and the answers use live prices, news and filings. You can also name the themes you care about, like AI infrastructure or nuclear power, and it follows the news on them.


### 4. Research ideas, then check the sources


AI is quick at reading filings, earnings releases and news, and at turning a rough idea into a short list of companies worth a closer look. Before you act, open the filing or article an answer cites, and be wary of any answer with no source.


After a short risk assessment, you and Astor agree on a target mix, and it recommends specific buys and sells, with dollar amounts, based on that target, everything you hold, your risk level, taxes and preferences. When you ask for new ideas, it leaves out what you already own and says why each name made the list. These are recommendations, and you decide whether to act on them.


### 5. Let it watch, on rules you set


Decide what would make you rethink a position, like an earnings report or a big price move, and set alerts for those instead of checking prices all day.


Astor follows every position you own. On Pro and Max, when news, earnings or a big move touches one of them, it texts you right away over iMessage or WhatsApp, and it stays quiet when nothing matters. On every plan you can set[scheduled alerts](https://www.astor.app/blog/scheduled-alerts) , like a check-in before a company you own reports. The free plan includes one custom alert at a time, plus a short recap after each close and a weekly review.


### 6. Make the call, and place the trade yourself


Keep the last step for yourself, and take it when you’re calm, since the SEC, NASAA and FINRA warn that chatbot conversations can lead to impulsive decisions. Before you let any tool near an order, find out whether it can trade without asking.


With Astor’s[Text to Trade](https://www.astor.app/blog/introducing-text-to-trade) , available on Max plans, you describe a trade or an idea in the app’s chat, and Astor proposes the orders and explains its reasoning. You approve each order on its own card, and it executes in your own Robinhood agentic account. The agent can only use the money you set aside for it, and nothing is bought until you approve. Astor can’t trade or move money in your other connected accounts.
